video_metadata.working_title: CALIFORNIA 1984 Cold Case Solved After 27 Years — Justice for Tina Faelz
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: In April 1984 a 14-year-old Foothill High freshman, Tina Faelz, was stabbed to death on a shortcut home under Interstate 680 in Pleasanton, California; 27 years later a trace of someone else's blood on her purse was linked by DNA to her classmate Steven Carlson, who was convicted in 2014 and confessed in letters in 2020.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into quiet outrage at how long the answer waited inside one small piece of evidence, then bittersweet partial justice

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Tina Faelz (victim, the heart of the story). Perpetrator: Steven John Carlson.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: Tina: 14. Carlson: 16 in April 1984; 43 at his arrest in August 2011; 46 at the verdict in October 2014.
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Tina: freshman at Foothill High School, Pleasanton. Carlson: fellow Foothill High student who lived on Lemonwood Way near the trail where she was found.
protagonist.location: Pleasanton, Alameda County, California; Tina lived in the Valley Trails neighborhood, east of Interstate 680.
protagonist.physical_description: Not documented in the sources consulted; use real archival photos only.
protagonist.background_brief: Tina lived with her mother, Shirley (later Shirley Faelz Orosco), and her younger brother Drew, who was 8 in 1984. Her mother said in 2008 that Tina had recently started walking home from school to avoid being teased by other students on the bus. Carlson was a Foothill student; after 1984 he built an extensive criminal record, including convictions reported by prosecutors for lewd acts with a child under 14 and for assault, and in 2011 he was in Santa Cruz County Jail on drug charges.
protagonist.psychological_profile: Carlson: in his 2020 letters he wrote that he remembered being full of rage, that he had been bullied over a house party he tried to throw at his parents' home, and that he had lived in denial for many years. A writer on the case told CBS that he was bullied but was also a major bully himself. No other profile is documented; do not speculate.
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: Tina chose to walk home, through a path by Aster Court and Lemonwood Way and the I-680 underpass, to escape teasing on the school bus. A lilac tree was later planted on the Foothill campus in her memory.

characters.name: Stacie Pettigrew
characters.role_in_story: Alameda County deputy district attorney who prosecuted Carlson
characters.key_actions_they_took: Built the case on the DNA from the blood on Tina's purse; told jurors the odds of the blood belonging to someone else were about 1 in 5 quadrillion; cited his prior convictions

characters.name: Annie Beles
characters.key_actions_they_took: Called the DNA evidence flimsy; questioned when and how it was collected, possible contamination and transfer; noted there was no motive, fingerprints or weapon
characters.notable_quotes: Described the DNA evidence as "flimsy" (single word attributed in summaries)

characters.name: Judge C. Don Clay
characters.role_in_story: Alameda County Superior Court judge at trial and sentencing
characters.key_actions_they_took: Denied the motion for a new trial and sentenced Carlson to 26 years to life in January 2015

characters.name: Judge Rhonda Burgess (per NBC Bay Area; Danville San Ramon credits Judge Trina Thompson)
characters.role_in_story: Juvenile court judge who ruled Carlson should be tried as an adult
characters.key_actions_they_took: Cited the criminal sophistication of the killing, the severity of the crime and previous failed attempts at rehabilitation

characters.name: Joshua Suchon
characters.role_in_story: Author of 'Murder in Pleasanton: Tina Faelz and the Search for Justice' (The History Press, 2015; audiobook with a new chapter, Tantor 2022)
characters.key_actions_they_took: Was a fifth grader at Donlon Elementary in April 1984; his sister knew Carlson; researched Carlson's life up to his arrest
characters.notable_quotes: "The thing that drew me to the story was my sister knew Steve Carlson."

characters.name: Pleasanton Police Department
characters.key_actions_they_took: Collected the evidence in 1984; re-examined it in late 2007 with new science, sending it to two laboratories; announced the DNA link in August 2011 and arrested Carlson

characters.role_in_story: Credited by CBS News with the DNA work that linked Carlson

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.what_happened: Foothill High School opens on the west side of Pleasanton (background, verify)
Tina starts walking home from Foothill High instead of taking the bus, to avoid being teased by other students
events.significance: The reason she was on the shortcut

events.what_happened: Tina is last seen alive after leaving school to walk home

events.location: Path via Aster Court and Lemonwood Way to the I-680 underpass, toward Valley Trails
events.what_happened: Tina is attacked and stabbed to death in a drainage culvert/ditch that crossed beneath Interstate 680, east of the school
Fellow students discover her body near the creek bed; her purse is found hanging in a tree near the scene
events.significance: Discovery; the purse is the evidence that matters 27 years later

events.what_happened: Apple's '1984' Macintosh commercial airs during the Super Bowl
Alec Jeffreys discovers DNA fingerprinting, five months after Tina's death
events.significance: Irony: the science that would solve the case was born the same year

events.what_happened: Colin Pitchfork becomes the first murderer convicted on DNA evidence
The FBI's national DNA index (NDIS, part of CODIS) begins operating
events.significance: Crime scene profiles can be searched nationally

events.what_happened: Voters pass Proposition 69, expanding DNA collection to all felony convicts and, from 2009, adult felony arrestees
Pleasanton police re-examine evidence collected in 1984 using analyses not available then, sending it to two laboratories
Pleasanton Weekly publishes the cover story 'Who killed Tina Faelz?'; her mother (interviewed in 2008) describes why Tina walked home
events.significance: The case is still public and unsolved after 24 years

events.what_happened: DNA testing shows a small amount of blood on Tina's purse that was not hers came from Steven Carlson; CBS credits the FBI crime lab (one report dates the match to 2007)
Pleasanton police take Carlson, 43, into custody from the jail where he was held on drug charges
Carlson is charged with murder in juvenile court because he was 16 at the time; he tells NBC Bay Area 'I didn't do it' and pleads not guilty
events.significance: Unusual legal path: a 43-year-old in juvenile court

events.what_happened: Carlson appears in court on the 1984 murder
Judge rules Carlson unfit for juvenile court and orders him tried as an adult, citing the sophistication and severity of the crime and failed attempts at rehabilitation
Tina's mother, Shirley Faelz Orosco, dies unexpectedly on the day the trial was originally scheduled to begin
Trial: prosecutor Stacie Pettigrew presents the DNA (odds about 1 in 5 quadrillion); defense attorney Annie Beles attacks collection and contamination and notes no motive, fingerprints or weapon
After about one day of deliberations, the jury convicts Carlson, 46, of first-degree murder
Judge C. Don Clay denies a new trial and sentences Carlson to 26 years to life; Carlson still professes innocence
The History Press publishes Joshua Suchon's 'Murder in Pleasanton: Tina Faelz and the Search for Justice'
A three-judge panel reduces the conviction to second-degree murder because prosecutors had not proved premeditation and deliberation; CBS reports the sentence became 16 years to life

Approaching his first parole hearing, Carlson writes a nine-page insight statement for parole commissioners, a letter to the Faelz family and a letter to Tina, admitting the killing; the family shares them with the San Francisco Chronicle; he then cancels his own parole hearing
Tantor releases the audiobook of 'Murder in Pleasanton' with a new chapter of case updates
Voters approve Proposition 57, ending prosecutors' direct filing of juveniles in adult court; transfer again requires a judge's hearing
events.significance: Legal context for the juvenile-court path

events.what_happened: No public report of a parole grant was found; CBS said his next hearing would be in three years and a low-reliability secondary source mentions 2027. Status to verify with CDCR inmate locator

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.exact_location: A footpath from Foothill High School past Aster Court and Lemonwood Way to a drainage culvert under Interstate 680, Pleasanton, California
the_moment.what_is_happening: A 14-year-old freshman walks home alone on a shortcut she has chosen to avoid teasing on the school bus
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: She was found within the hour by fellow students; the killer was a classmate who lived on the very street her path crossed, and he stayed free for 27 years
the_moment.ironic_twist: Her purse, hung in a tree near the scene, held a trace of his blood the whole time; five months after her death, in England, Alec Jeffreys discovered DNA fingerprinting

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed a 14-year-old girl in broad daylight on a walk home, and why did the answer take 27 years?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
the_method.technique_name: Modern STR DNA profiling of a trace bloodstain from 1984 evidence (the victim's purse), compared against a known profile
step_by_step_explanation: 1984: police collect the purse found hanging in a tree near the scene and keep it in evidence
Late 2007: police re-examine the 1984 evidence with methods unavailable in 1984 and send items to two labs
Testing finds a trace of blood on the purse that is not Tina's
A DNA profile from that blood is linked to Steven Carlson (CBS credits the FBI crime lab; reports date the link to 2011)
At trial the prosecution says the chance the blood belongs to someone else is about 1 in 5 quadrillion
the_method.why_it_worked: The purse was preserved for decades, and DNA methods became sensitive enough to type a very small stain

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: A set of number readings at specific places in the DNA, like a barcode, that almost never repeats between unrelated people
The chance that a random unrelated person would share the same barcode; here about 1 in 5 quadrillion
The FBI-run system that lets labs compare crime-scene DNA against profiles of offenders
The defense theory that DNA can arrive on an item innocently or through handling, rather than during the crime

the_method.scale_of_operation: One trace stain on one item

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: No single institutional failure is documented; the main enemy was time and the limits of 1984 forensic science
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: No witnesses, no weapon, no fingerprints; DNA profiling did not exist in April 1984
specific_incompetence_examples: Not documented; do not invent. Open question: whether Carlson, who lived on the street the path crossed, was interviewed in 1984 (verify in Suchon's book)
The re-examination came in late 2007, about nine years after the national DNA index began operating in 1998
From re-examination (late 2007) to arrest (August 2011): almost four years
Arrest to verdict: more than three years; Tina's mother died on the day the trial was originally scheduled to begin
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The court of appeal found premeditation unproven; in 2020 Carlson wrote that he had taken a butcher knife from the kitchen before the attack

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Pleasanton Police Department; FBI laboratory credited; Alameda County District Attorney's Office prosecuted
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Not documented in the sources consulted
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: A trace of blood on Tina's purse that was not hers matched Carlson's DNA
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: He left his own blood on her purse

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.location: Santa Cruz County Jail, where Carlson was held on drug charges
the_confrontation.scene_description: Pleasanton police take custody of Carlson, 43, and bring him to Alameda County
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: Denied it: an NBC Bay Area headline quoted him, 'I didn't do it'; pleaded not guilty; professed innocence at sentencing in 2015
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: A 43-year-old man was charged in juvenile court because he was 16 at the time of the crime

charges_filed: Murder (Penal Code 187), initially in juvenile court, then in adult court after a fitness ruling
legal_resolution.trial_date_if_applicable: October 2014, Alameda County Superior Court; verdict October 30, 2014
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Prosecutor: blood on purse is Carlson's, odds of another source about 1 in 5 quadrillion. Defense: DNA flimsy, possible contamination or transfer, no motive, fingerprints or weapon. Oxygen reports a former friend testified Carlson was bullied and thrown into a dumpster after a confrontation with football players (single source).

victim_impact_statements.from_whom: Karin Reiff, Tina's aunt (statement after Shirley's death, not in court)
victim_impact_statements.key_quote: "My sister went through almost 30 years of hell after Tina's death and I think she finally died of a broken heart."

legal_resolution.sentence_received: 26 years to life (January 9, 2015); after the 2017 appeal reduced the conviction to second-degree murder, 16 years to life (CBS)
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: Professed innocence at sentencing (CBS headline 'Professing innocence, man gets 26 years to life')
legal_resolution.current_status: Convicted of second-degree murder; incarcerated at the California Correctional Institution, Tehachapi (as last reported). No public record found of parole being granted as of October 2026; verify with CDCR.
